narrative:
## Handover Summary — NII Baseline

The FY2026 NII baseline is locked at PLN 3.33B across the combined VeloBank + ex-Citi balance sheet.

## Key Decisions
- Affluent & Private Banking uplifted to reflect 94% ex-Citi balance retention
- SME / Business Banking raised on working-capital volume momentum
- Retail consumer lending in the South raised on Citi cardholder cross-sell

## Recommendation for NBP Rate Scenarios
ALM should stress this baseline against dovish and hawkish NBP paths. Priority: quantify sensitivity of the ex-Citi deposit base, where behavioural assumptions are least proven.

## Risk Factors
- Deposit outflow if VeloBank cuts rates faster than peers
- Integration cost and restructuring of up to 950 roles running alongside the plan

signals.title: Citi Handlowy Retail Integration Completed
signals.excerpt: Migration of the Citi Handlowy retail business completed on 15 June 2026: PLN 22.1B of deposits, PLN 6B of loans, PLN 8.9B AuM and ~1,600 employees now on VeloBank systems.

signals.title: Management Commentary — Rate Headwind
signals.excerpt: Management flagged NBP rate cuts as the key earnings headwind for net interest income, with deposit pricing discipline and balance-sheet growth as offsets.
